newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM gold firms, shrugging off Hashimoto remark.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM gold firms, shrugging off Hashimoto remark.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo gold futures firmed slightly in early trade on Tuesday, with little impact from reported remarks by Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto that Japan might be tempted to sell U.S. government bonds and switch foreign reserves to gold, Japanese traders said.
Benchmark April gold was up three yen at 1,247 yen in early morning trade.

"The remark doesn't mean Japan's government would buy gold. The comment wouldn't be enough to make gold rise sharply," a trader said. Spot gold was quoted at $339.85/340.15 in early morning, against $339.10/60 in late New York on Monday.
